I am writing to raise a serious complaint regarding the poor level of customer service I experienced at your KFC branch located at Lidl Retail Park, New Nangor Road, Clondalkin, Dublin 22, D22 F638.

On Thursday, 16th of May 2025, at approximately 9:20 PM, I was refused access to the restroom by staff who claimed it was already being cleaned. This was incredibly frustrating and disappointing, especially considering that the restaurant operates until 10:00 PM. Restroom facilities should be available to paying customers up to closing time. I clearly explained that I urgently needed to use the bathroom and even stated that I was only going to urinate, yet I was still met with the excuse: “I’m changing the toilet paper and replacing the soap, so you can’t come in for the rest of the night.” I fail to see how that reasoning would prevent someone from using the toilet for such a basic and brief need.

Not only is this reasoning unreasonable, it also raises significant hygiene concerns. By preventing customers from accessing the restroom, you are also denying them access to washing facilities—which is essential, particularly in a food service environment. This compromises health and safety standards for everyone. Additionally, preventing a customer from using restroom facilities could potentially pose health risks and should never be standard practice.

Despite being a paying customer, I was treated with a lack of courtesy and understanding. Unfortunately, this is not the first time I’ve had a negative experience at this branch. Previous visits have included order mistakes—such as missing items like gravy—and consistently poor customer service. The staff have been unkind, dismissive, and unwilling to help.

This most recent incident left me genuinely unhappy and dissatisfied. It was an upsetting experience that I believe reflects poorly on the KFC brand. If this is the standard of service being provided, it risks damaging the franchise's reputation among customers like myself.

As a final point, I would like to note that while restaurants in Ireland are not legally required to provide public toilets, once a business chooses to offer restroom facilities—as KFC Clondalkin does—those facilities should remain accessible to paying customers during advertised opening hours. Refusing access before closing time, especially without operational urgency, could raise concerns under health and safety obligations and consumer protection standards in Ireland.

I strongly encourage KFC management to review the practices at this location and ensure that all staff are properly trained to provide respectful, hygienic, and professional service at all times.
